Comme à Gaza ou pour l’Iran, seul Donald Trump parvient à limiter l’usage de la force militaire par Israël. lemonde.title: Génocide des Tutsi : « La seule chose que l’on puisse offrir aux Rwandais, c’est la vérité sur cette terrible tragédie dont la France a été partie prenante »

france24fr.title: RD Congo : attaque meurtrière des rebelles de l'ADF à Beni, dans l'est du pays.
france24fr.description: Dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo, les rebelles ADF, affilié à l’État islamique, ont mené une attaque dans la ville de Beni. Ces rebelles commettent des massacres à répétition mais, c’est la première fois depuis plus de trois ans que les ADF frappent à l’intérieur de la ville, un signe préoccupant. Les précisions avec notre correspondante à Kinshasa, Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula.

france24fr.title: L'UE autorise la création de "hubs de retour" à l'étranger pour les migrants illégaux
france24fr.description: Le Parlement européen a donné son feu vert lundi soir pour la création de centres pour le renvoi de migrants à l'étranger. Ces "hubs de retour" dans des pays intermédiaires sont championnés par l'Allemagne, alors que l'Espagne y voit une menace pour le respect des droits humains.

france24fr.title: Kenya : colère contre l’accueil de patients américains atteints d’Ebola
france24fr.description: Au Kenya, des centaines de personnes ont manifesté à Nanyuki, une ville du centre du pays, contre la mise en place d’un centre de quarantaine dédié aux citoyens américains exposés au virus Ebola. Deux personnes ont été tuées dans ces manifestations.

france24fr.title: Législatives en Arménie : les autorités évoquent des ingérences russes avant les élections
france24fr.description: Cinq jours avant les élections législatives en Arménie, le Premier ministre, Nikol Pachinian, a rejeté lundi l'appel du président russe Vladimir Poutine à organiser un référendum sur une adhésion de l'Arménie à l'UE, affirmant que les relations avec la Russie étaient dans une "phase de transformation".

france24fr.title: Bombardements intenses en Ukraine : au moins quatre morts à Kiev
france24fr.description: La Russie a tiré sur l'Ukraine plus de 600 drones et des dizaines de missiles, dont des missiles balistiques plus difficiles à déjouer par la défense antiaérienne, a indiqué mardi l'armée de l'air ukrainienne après une nuit dont le bilan est de plusieurs morts. Les habitants se sont réfugiés dans les stations de métro. "Je n'ai jamais vu une station de métro aussi pleine" racontre notre correspondant, Gulliver Cragg, depuis la capitale ukrainienne.

france24fr.title: Ebola : deux morts dans des manifestations au Kenya contre des centres d'isolement américains
france24fr.description: Des centaines de manifestants se sont rassemblés lundi ​à Nanyuki, ville du centre du Kenya, pour protester contre le projet des Etats-Unis d'instaurer un centre de ​quarantaine pour les personnes potentiellement infectées par le virus Ebola, ont déclaré à Reuters des habitants. Deux personnes ont été tuées dans ces manifestations.

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : au moins quatre morts à Kiev après des frappes de missiles russes
france24fr.description: La Russie a tiré sur l'Ukraine plus de 600 drones et des dizaines de missiles, dont des missiles balistiques plus difficiles à déjouer par la défense antiaérienne, a indiqué mardi l'armée de l'air ukrainienne après une nuit dont le bilan est de plusieurs morts.

france24fr.title: Premier président d'extrême droite au Chili : José Antonio Kast amorce son mandat
france24fr.description: Le président chilien d'extrême droite José Antonio Kast a annoncé lundi, lors de son premier discours de politique générale devant le Parlement, diverses mesures, notamment sur le plan sécuritaire, pour tenter d'endiguer sa chute de popularité trois mois à peine après son arrivée au pouvoir.

france24fr.title: Au Liban, l'ONU veut maintenir ses troupes après 2026
france24fr.description: Le secrétaire général de l'ONU a recommandé lundi de maintenir des troupes onusiennes au Liban après le départ fin 2026 de la force de maintien de la paix actuelle, une option qui risque de se heurter à l'opposition des Etats-Unis et d'Israël.

france24fr.title: Course aux drones entre Kiev et Moscou : chute d'un drone sur un immeuble en Roumanie
france24fr.description: Plus de 56 pays, notamment membres de l'Union européenne et de l'Otan, ont dénoncé lundi à l'ONU le comportement “inacceptable” de la Russie après la chute d'un drone sur un immeuble en Roumanie la semaine dernière, selon une déclaration lue par la ministre roumaine des Affaires étrangères. Les précisions avec notre invité, Paul Vallet, politologue et chercheur associé Centre de Sécurité Politique de Genève.

france24fr.title: Immigration : "L'UE dans les pas de Donald Trump ?"
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce mardi 2 juin, le feu vert de l’UE, pour la création de centres en dehors d’Europe pour y accueillir des migrants illégaux. Le rejet, par la justice, d'une demande d’indemnisation du Rwanda, après l’annulation d'un accord d’asile conclu avec le Royaume-Uni. L’essor, en France, des data centers, essentiels à l’intelligence artificielle. Une course dans laquelle s’est aussi engagée la Chine, où modernisation rime avec répression. Et un drôle de procès intenté à Brad Pitt.

france24fr.title: Roland-Garros : Aryna Sabalenka reine de la "night session" face à Osaka
france24fr.description: Aryna Sabalenka n’a pas tremblé face à Naomi Osaka (7-5, 6-3) en huitièmes de finale à Roland-Garros. Elle affrontera la Russe Diana Shnaider au tour suivant.

france24fr.title: En direct : nouveaux affrontements entre Israël et le Hezbollah avant une reprise des négociations
france24fr.description: Israël et le Hezbollah ont poursuivi leurs affrontements dans la nuit de lundi à mardi malgré l'annonce par Donald Trump de l'accord des deux camps pour cesser les hostilités avant un nouveau cycle de négociations entre Libanais et Israéliens mardi à Washington. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Génocide des Tutsi au Rwanda : un monument en mémoire des victimes inauguré à Paris
france24fr.description: Un monument à la mémoire des victimes du génocide au Rwanda est inauguré mardi sur les quais de Seine, en plein cœur de Paris, par les présidents français Emmanuel Macron et rwandais Paul Kagame. Conçue par l'artiste portugaise Grada Kilomba, cette double stèle servira de "lieu de recueillement, en souvenir des disparus, et de transmission intergénérationnelle de la mémoire du génocide", selon l'Élysée.

france24fr.title: Boualem Sansal publie "La Légende", un "livre de combat" contre l'Algérie et ses critiques
france24fr.description: Dans "La Légende", publié mardi, l'écrivain franco-algérien Boualem Sansal revient sur sa détention en Algérie et répond à ses critiques. L'ouvrage paraît quelques semaines après la polémique suscitée par son départ de Gallimard, son éditeur historique, au profit de Grasset, maison d'édition du groupe Hachette situé dans l'orbite du milliardaire Vincent Bolloré.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : des attaques russes meurtrières visent Kiev, Dnipro et Kharkiv
france24fr.description: La Russie a annoncé mardi avoir mené dans la nuit une "frappe massive" contre des sites du complexe militaro-industriel à travers l'Ukraine avec des "armes de haute précision", y compris des missiles hypersoniques. Selon les autorités ukrainiennes, l'attaque a fait 13 morts, dont quatre dans la capitale Kiev, et une soixantaine de blessés.

france24fr.title: Les spationautes français Thomas Pesquet et Arnaud Prost partiront dans l'espace en 2027
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron a annoncé lundi que deux astronautes français partiraient dans l'espace en 2027 dans le cadre d'un accord signé avec l'entreprise américaine Vast. Le célèbre Thomas Pesquet partira en tant que commandant de vol pour l'ISS où il a déjà séjourné deux fois, tandis qu'Arnaud Prost se rendra dans la station spatiale commerciale Haven-1.

spiegel.description: Als Favorit reiste das DFB-Team zur WM 1994 – und flog im Viertelfinale raus. Eine Dokumentation seziert das deutsche Chaosturnier. Im Mittelpunkt: Trainer Berti Vogts und drei Weltmeister von 1990, die ihm in den Rücken fielen.

spiegel.title: Manuel Neuer: Wie der Weltmeister ein eigenes Firmenimperium aufbaut
spiegel.description: Manuel Neuer ist mit 40 noch immer ein Weltklasse-Torhüter. Nebenbei betätigt er sich als Unternehmer. Kaffee, Kosmetik, Putzmittel, Radsport: das Firmengeflecht im Überblick.

spiegel.title: Annalena Baerbock: Präsidentin der Uno-Generalversammlung fordert Reformen
spiegel.description: Für die Präsidentin der Uno-Generalversammlung gibt es keine Alternative zu den Vereinten Nationen. Vor zwei wichtigen Wahlen plädiert sie jedoch für harte Reformen. Und ein Bekenntnis zum Völkerrecht.

spiegel.title: China hat Tausende deutscher Patente übernommen
spiegel.description: Innovationen aus Deutschland wandern immer häufiger in chinesischen Besitz. Eine Auswertung zeigt, wie viele Erfindungen inzwischen in ausländischer Hand sind. Vor allem ein Industriezweig ist betroffen.

spiegel.title: Rente: Bärbel Bas will Beamte in Rentenversicherung einbeziehen - wie sinnvoll ist das?
spiegel.description: SPD-Arbeitsministerin Bärbel Bas fordert, dass künftig auch Beamte in die gesetzliche Rente einzahlen. Das hätte viele Vorteile. Einen drohenden Finanzkollaps wird das jedoch nicht abwenden.

spiegel.title: CDU und CSU und Kommunikation: Gefährliche Arroganz - Kommentar
spiegel.description: Die Union steckt im Umfragetief. Ein Grund dürfte auch der kalte Tonfall sein, den manche in CDU und CSU anschlagen. Das schadet der einzigen bürgerlichen Volkspartei, die dieses Land hat.

spiegel.title: Durchschnittsmensch in Deutschland: So groß und schwer sind Erwachsene im Schnitt
spiegel.description: Mehr als die Hälfte der Erwachsenen in Deutschland ist übergewichtig. Das geht aus den Daten des Statistischen Bundesamts hervor. Bei Männern ist das Problem größer.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Almuth Schult über US-Aufenthalt und Fragen nach der Kinderbetreuung
spiegel.description: Eine Fußball-WM in Übersee muss gut geplant werden, auch von Journalisten und Kommentatorinnen. Die ehemalige Nationalkeeperin Almuth Schult bereitet sich akribisch vor – und wundert sich über manche Fragen.

spiegel.title: Israel – Libanon: Trump will Konflikt entschärfen – Iran droht mit Konsequenzen
spiegel.description: Iran droht wegen der israelischen Angriffe im Libanon mit dem Abbruch der Verhandlungen mit den USA. Was US-Präsident Trump zu einem Anruf bei Premier Netanyahu und deutlichen Worten bewogen haben soll.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Polizei in Mexiko setzt Tränengas an Fan-Meile gegen Demonstranten ein
spiegel.description: Kurz vor Beginn der Fußball-WM haben in Mexiko-Stadt Zusammenstöße zwischen der Polizei und demonstrierenden Lehrkräften für Aufsehen gesorgt. Letztere wollten sich Zugang zu einer im Aufbau befindlichen Fanzone verschaffen.

spiegel.title: CDU/CSU und SPD: Konsenskränzchen mit Arbeitgebern und Gewerkschaften? Das wird nicht gutgehen
spiegel.description: Die Regierung will alle an einen Tisch holen, damit es mit der Wirtschaft vorangeht. Doch schon das historische Vorbild dieser Idee hat nicht funktioniert.

spiegel.title: Taylor Swift singt in »Toy Story 5«: »I Knew It, I Knew You«
spiegel.description: Die Abenteuer um die Spielzeugfiguren Woody und Buzz Lightyear hat sie als 5-Jährige geliebt. Jetzt erfüllt sich Taylor Swift einen Traum – und schreibt einen Song für die fünfte Fortsetzung.

spiegel.title: Sportfan Melinda French Gates steigt bei den Seattle Kraken ein
spiegel.description: Gewöhnlich gibt Melinda French Gates ihre Milliarden für gemeinnützige Zwecke aus. Ihr jüngstes Investment gilt aber einem Club in der weltweit besten Hockeyliga – und womöglich kommt bald eine weitere Sportart hinzu.

spiegel.title: Sylt: Betonvordach stürzt in Westerland auf den Bürgersteig
spiegel.description: Ein lauter Knall schreckt die Nachbarn auf: Mitten in Westerland bricht das Vordach eines Gebäudes ab. Verletzte gibt es nicht – aber eine Vermutung zur Ursache des Vorfalls.

spiegel.title: Rheinmetall: Vom Schmuddelkind zum Champion der deutschen Rüstungsindustrie
spiegel.description: Der Waffenhersteller Rheinmetall hat schon oft von kriegerischen Zeiten profitiert. Aber selten lief es so gut wie heute. Fürs Geschäft waren die Verantwortlichen immer wieder bereit, an moralische Grenzen zu gehen.

spiegel.title: Hamburg: Mann in Supermarkt niedergestochen
spiegel.description: In einem Laden in Hamburg-Altona hat ein Mann einen anderen mit einem Messer tödlich verletzt. Der Tat soll ein Streit vorausgegangen sein. Der Verdächtige wurde festgenommen.

observador.title: Confrontos violentos entre jovens em Cascais fazem 2 feridos
observador.description: Incidente ocorreu na madrugada de domingo numas festas populares. Dois grupos rivais envolveram-se numa rixa, um dos jovens terá continuado a ser espancado já depois de perder a consciência.

observador.title: Depressão: tratar mais cedo, mais perto e melhor
observador.description: A depressão custa mais de mil milhões de euros por ano em Portugal. Mais do que números, são vidas e projetos adiados. Hoje há mais respostas, mas o acesso continua muitas vezes tardio e desigual.

observador.title: Mercedes-Benz Stadium, o estádio mais moderno do mundo
observador.description: A cobertura é o elemento mais diferenciador de um Mercedes-Benz Stadium que tem o arco central inspirado no Panteão de Roma e mais de 180 obras de arte. Beyoncé é exemplo de sucesso no estádio.

observador.title: "Basta um herdeiro para desbloquear a venda de um imóvel"
observador.description: João Vale e Azevedo afirma que basta um herdeiro para forçar a venda judicial de imóveis que se encontram bloqueados. Ainda acrescenta que a medida visa colocar milhares de habitações no mercado.

observador.title: Portugal continental com vento e descida de temperatura
observador.description: Rajadas de vento podem chegar aos 70 km/h e descida de temperatura variar entre 3 e 6/7 graus. Meteorologista Maria João Frada diz ser uma situação normal no mês de junho.

observador.title: Movimento promove transição democrática na Venezuela
observador.description: Proposta foi divulgada através de um "manifesto cidadão" que defende que "a recuperação institucional do país passa por devolver aos venezuelanos a possibilidade de eleger livremente as autoridades".

observador.title: Foxconn alia-se à Bull para desenvolver IA na Europa
observador.description: Colaboração permitirá consolidar em França uma cadeia de abastecimento local para inteligência artificial e capacidade de computação, com o objetivo de criar um "ecossistema europeu de IA soberana".

observador.title: Elevador Glória: Carris está a trabalhar para sair por cima
observador.description: Rui Lopo, que assumiu a presidência do Conselho de Administração (CA) da transportadora Carris após o anterior CA ter renunciado aos cargos, reitera uma total cooperação com as autoridades.

observador.title: "Espero ficar até dia 19 para trazermos a taça", diz Velho
observador.description: A nove dias do arranque do Campeonato do Mundo, Ricardo Velho voltou a reforçar a ambição de conquistar a competição. Seleção treina sem os quatro bicampeões da Europa. Siga aqui em direto.

observador.title: Índia e Estados Unidos perto de um acordo comercial
observador.description: Depois da guerra tarifária e das sanções impostas pelos EUA aos compradores de petróleo russo, que dura há meses, ministro do Comércio indiano afirmou que acordo bilateral está muito perto.

observador.title: Rangel aponta "construção de pontes" como trunfo de Portugal
observador.description: Ministro assegura que Portugal está bem posicionado para conquistar um quarto mandato como membro não permanente do Conselho de Segurança e garante que a campanha prosseguirá até ao último momento.

observador.title: PSP deteve homem condenado a 11 anos no aeroporto de Lisboa
observador.description: PSP esclarece que homem foi condenado por roubo qualificado, violação e sequestro, tendo sido conduzido ao Estabelecimento Prisional de Lisboa para cumprimento da pena de 11 anos de prisão.

observador.title: Sindicato critica ULS Alto Ave por proibir férias de médicos
observador.description: ULS do Alto Ave proibiu os médicos de Medicina Geral e Familiar de gozarem férias, que estavam acordadas, entre 19 e 31 de dezembro. Decisão surge após o anúncio da adesão dos médicos à greve geral.

observador.title: Santa Casa apela por famílias de acolhimento em Lisboa
observador.description: Em comunicado, a instituição explica que existem atualmente mais de mil crianças no distrito de Lisboa à procura de uma família de acolhimento.

observador.title: 9h. Salários. Governo ainda não aplicou regras de Bruxelas
observador.description: O prazo termina este domingo e o Governo diz que medidas ainda estão a ser ultimadas. Ainda os avisos de Cavaco Silva ao Governo e um ponto de situação do conflito no Médio Oriente.

observador.title: Plano prevê 500 milhões por ano até 2030 para natureza
observador.description: Plano Nacional de Restauro da Natureza, apresentado pelo Governo esta terça-feira, prevê plantação de três milhões de árvores por ano até 2030. Engloba ainda medidas a nível marinho, fluvial e urbano.

observador.title: A reforma do Estado é apenas uma miragem desde 1978?
observador.description: Cavaco Silva reclama razão eterna contra burocratas, enquanto Mário Centeno faz "preço certo" das contas. Entre o mofo de 1978 e a vaidade do superávit, Estado continua à espera de uma reforma a sério

observador.title: IATA afasta risco de falta de combustível para aviação
observador.description: Apesar de afastar, para já, o risco de falta de combustível no verão, a IATA alerta para o impacto do aumento dos custos nos preços das viagens aéreas

elpais.title: Junts reta a Feijóo a reunirse en Waterloo con Puigdemont para plantear la moción de censura
elpais.description: El secretario general del partido independentista catalán sale al paso de la invitación que lanzó Alberto Núñez Feijóo para desbancar a Pedro Sánchez

elpais.title: Sánchez cuestiona ante su cúpula el trato de la justicia al PSOE
elpais.description: La portavoz de la dirección socialista subraya que la UCO ya ha hecho dos informes sobre Begoña Gómez y todavía ninguno del novio de Ayuso

elpais.title: Los datos de precios y compras de vivienda reflejan un mercado al límite en el arranque del año
elpais.description: Los expertos apuntan a las primeras señales de un cambio de signo, aunque solo vaticinan un giro brusco si se agravan los conflictos bélicos

elpais.title: Familias que sufren con la Selectividad: “Me da igual la nota, lo único que quiero es que se acabe ya la PAU”
elpais.description: El estrés de los progenitores ante la prueba de acceso a la universidad crece en paralelo al aumento de las notas de corte

elpais.title: Mapa de sitios oficiales para ver el eclipse total de Sol: EL PAÍS actualiza el único buscador de puntos de observación
elpais.description: España se enfrenta al reto de acoger a millones de visitantes el 12 de agosto. Ayuntamientos y autonomías ya han elegido 190 miradores para gestionar concentraciones multitudinarias para contemplar el histórico fenómeno

elpais.title: Presunta imparcialidad
elpais.description: El doble rasero judicial y policial acaba erosionando la legitimidad de un poder fundamental del Estado

elpais.title: Las reinas no fuman
elpais.description: El mensaje general de doña Letizia casi parecía dirigido a alguien en particular

elpais.description: La ofensiva del Kremlin golpea Kiev, Dnipró y Járkov y causa un centenar de heridos

elpais.title: Las banderas ultras de Abelardo de la Espriella
elpais.description: El vencedor de la primera vuelta, que ha empleado un tono misógino y homofóbico, es admirador de Milei y Bukele, promete recortar un 40% de la burocracia del Estado y quiere volver a debatir derechos que ya han ganado las mujeres y la población LGBTI frente al aborto y la adopción de niños

elpais.title: El triunfo de De la Espriella, “una derecha populista que promete soluciones fáciles a problemas supercomplejos”
elpais.description: El candidato ultra logra el 43,7% de los votos frente al 40,9% de Iván Cepeda, el aspirante de izquierda, en la primera vuelta

elpais.title: Etgar Keret, escritor: “Si la vida es una película, Israel es hoy una de zombis”
elpais.description: El narrador mira a la cotidianidad con humor negro y surrealismo en la colección de relatos ‘El blues del fin del mundo’. El ataque de Hamás en 2023 retrasó su publicación

elpais.title: Jonathan Andic da la batalla de la opinión pública con la vista puesta ya en el jurado popular
elpais.description: El primogénito de Isak Andic, investigado por el presunto homicidio de su padre, fía la misión de revertir el relato a un investigador privado de la defensa

elpais.title: Los destinos turísticos españoles empiezan a bajar precios ante el freno de reservas para verano
elpais.description: Los viajeros extranjeros retrasan las contrataciones a la espera de ofertas de última hora o barajan quedarse en sus lugares de origen por los costes de volar y alojarse en otros países

elpais.title: El Gobierno suspende el contrato de ciberseguridad del Estado por falta de fondos
elpais.description: El Ministerio para la Transformación Digital paraliza la adjudicación que ganó Telefónica tras un accidentado proceso de licitación con tres cambios de compañía

elpais.title: La economía gana 232.000 empleos en mayo, el mayor impulso en ocho años, pero la caída del paro se resiente
elpais.description: La afiliación total alcanza un nuevo récord de 22,3 millones, con un fuerte avance de los extranjeros. El desempleo registrado retrocede en 36.300 personas, uno de los peores registros en ese mes desde 2012

elpais.title: La UE reafirma el endurecimiento de su política migratoria al validar la creación de centros de deportación en terceros países
elpais.description: El Consejo y el Parlamento Europeo acuerdan los términos del nuevo reglamento de retornos que allana el camino para enviar a los migrantes rechazados a terceros países fuera de la UE, incluidas familias con menores

elpais.title: La inminente llegada de ‘El Niño’ echará “más leña al fuego de un mundo que se calienta”
elpais.description: La Organización Meteorológica Mundial insta a estar preparados ante el riesgo de aumento de los fenómenos extremos con la aparición de este evento natural

nyt.title: Iran War Live Updates: Israel Appears to Pull Back From Threat to Strike Beirut
nyt.description: President Trump is pressing Israel not to attack the Lebanese capital. An escalation in Israel’s campaign against Hezbollah could threaten peace talks with Iran.

nyt.title: Trump Backs Off Plan for $1.8 Billion Fund That Drew Political Backlash
nyt.description: The fund has drawn backlash from critics who said it was a scheme to reward President Trump’s political allies with public benefits.

nyt.title: Losing Trust in Justice Dept., Judges Call Out Its Lawyers’ Behavior
nyt.description: The federal courts have long assumed that the government’s lawyers are trustworthy. Now judges across the country are criticizing their lack of candor.

nyt.title: Trump Targets Brazil With 25% Tariff, Citing Unfair Trade Practices
nyt.description: The proposal marks the latest effort by the administration to rebuild its tariff agenda through Section 301 investigations.

nyt.title: Trump Finds High-Wire Iran Negotiations ‘Very Boring’
nyt.description: President Trump told CNBC that he “couldn’t care less” if the negotiations with Iran break down.

nyt.title: Security Council Members Call for Israel to Withdraw From Southern Lebanon
nyt.description: The U.N. panel met after Israel had threatened to attack southern Beirut. President Trump said later that Israel and Hezbollah had agreed not to attack each other.

nyt.title: U.S. Says More People May Be Charged in Terror Case Linked to Iran
nyt.description: A militia leader pleaded not guilty on Monday to what prosecutors say is his role in attacks that are part of Iran’s response to the war with Israel and the United States.

nyt.title: Russia Launches Deadly Strikes on Ukraine
nyt.description: Missiles and drones struck the cities of Kyiv and Dnipro, Ukrainian officials said. At least 10 people were killed.

nyt.title: Anthropic Files to Go Public, Setting Stage for Huge I.P.O.
nyt.description: The artificial intelligence company, which is racing OpenAI to the stock market, has seen explosive growth over the last year thanks largely to technology that can automatically write computer code.

nyt.title: California’s Public Universities Went All in on A.I. Now They’re Tearing Themselves Apart.
nyt.description: California’s public universities spent $16.9 million on A.I. during a financial crisis, and the result has been chaos.

nyt.title: Scott Pelley Accuses CBS News Boss of ‘Murdering’ ‘60 Minutes’
nyt.description: In an explosive staff meeting, Mr. Pelley, a correspondent for the long-running Sunday news show, blasted Bari Weiss, the CBS editor in chief, and Nick Bilton, the show’s new executive producer.

nyt.title: The Return of Blaming and Shaming in Public Health
nyt.description: For years, medicine has tried to eliminate stigma. Now, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is bringing back the language of personal responsibility.

nyt.title: Minnesota Republicans Hold Moment of Silence for Derek Chauvin
nyt.description: Delegates to the Minnesota Republican Party’s convention voted to hold a moment of silence for Derek Chauvin, who was convicted of murdering George Floyd.

nyt.title: Obesity May Be More Prevalent Than Previously Thought
nyt.description: A new study suggests using body mass index alone may miss many people with the disease, but the findings come with caveats.

nyt.title: Mills Reminds Maine Voters She’s ‘Still on the Ballot’ for Senate Amid Platner Controversy
nyt.description: A month after withdrawing from the state’s Senate race, Gov. Janet Mills suggested she remained an option after the likely Democratic nominee, Graham Platner, faced a new scandal.

nyt.title: Previewing California’s Primary Elections and High-Stakes Governor’s Race
nyt.description: The deep-blue state’s primary elections will show how angry voters are at the status quo.

nyt.title: As Ebola Spreads, Scientists Race to Find Vaccines and Treatments
nyt.description: The Bundibugyo virus, a little known type, previously had caused just two small outbreaks. Now it’s at the center of a rapidly widening epidemic in Africa.

nyt.title: What to Know About the Ebola Outbreak
nyt.description: Aid agencies are racing to help health workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The virus is known to have killed at least 43, but the true toll may be far higher.

republika.description: Almeno tredici morti, tra cui un bambino

republika.description: L’ex direttrice di RtFrance è stata ingaggiata dalle tv della galassia del miliardario: “Segno di pluralismo”. Ma per per il ministro degli Esteri Barrot è un favore a Putin. Glucksmann: “Toglietele il microfono, è una agente”

republika.description: La deroga verrà illustrata domani in occasione della presentazione delle raccomandazioni economiche di primavera

republika.description: Il drammatico caso di Henry Nowak, accoltellato a morte da un 23enne sikh a Southampton. L’assassino millanta alla polizia di essere vittima di un’aggressione razzista e gli agenti arrestano il ragazzo in fin di vita, che spira ammanettato dicendo “I can’t breathe”, come George Floyd a Minneapolis nel 2020. Furia di Farage e della destra inglese: “Una vergogna, sono i bianchi ormai a essere discriminati: questo è razzismo al contrario”

republika.title: Arnaldi il maratoneta: “Ho giocato più al Roland Garros che in tutto l’anno”
republika.description: L'azzurro dopo il match epico con Tiafoe ripercorre una stagione complicata da un infortunio al piede: “Ho iniziato davvero a Cagliari, il mese scorso, ma prima aveva fatto tre giorni di allenamento”

republika.title: La strage dei braccianti pakistani, uccisi in auto e poi dati alle fiamme. Fermate due persone
republika.description: Il rogo in una stazione di servizio sulla statale 106 nei pressi di Amendolara, nel Cosentino. Determinanti i filmati delle telecamere di videosorveglianza: “Chiuse le portiere, arsi vivi in macchina”

republika.title: Italia, quarti di nobiltà al Roland Garros. Cobolli, Berrettini e la notte di Arnaldi
republika.description: Flavio supera Svajda e affronterà Auger-Aliassime. Derby tra i due Matteo: uno elimina Cerundolo, l'altro rimonta Tiafoe al 5°

republika.title: Vacanze in salute: dai pulsanti dell’ascensore alle maniglie, il decalogo per evitare virus
republika.description: Tutte le regole per non rischiare di contagiarsi il primo giorno di viaggio. L’elenco dei punti più contaminati nella hall degli hotel

republika.title: John Travolta: “La vita mi ha messo alla prova ma non mi arrendo”
republika.description: Il divo di Hollywood al suo esordio da regista con “Volo notturno per Los Angeles” ora su AppleTv, racconta il successo di “Pulp Fiction” e il ruolo fondamentale della sua famiglia. E confessa “’La strada’ di Fellini mi segnò, mi fece capire che non avrei mai spezzato il cuore a nessuno”

republika.title: Da suddite a cittadine, il 2 giugno delle donne
republika.description: Come si arrivò al voto alle donne di ottant’anni fa nel referendum che suggellò la nascita della Repubblica? Lo racconta oggi la storica al festival La grande invasione di Ivrea. Ecco un estratto del suo intervento

republika.title: Kiev brucia. I russi mobilitano una forza d’assalto colossale contro l’Ucraina
republika.description: Mosca aveva annunciato un’offensiva “senza precedenti” contro la capitale, ma l’attacco è stato esteso a tutto il Paese

republika.description: Arnaldi, Berrettini e Cobolli, mai nella storia del tennis tre italiani erano arrivati insieme ai quarti di finale di uno slam.

republika.title: Arnaldi e la Repubblica del talento
republika.description: il tennis ha trovato le risorse per fare a meno del suo centro narrativo con Arnaldi, Cobolli e Berrettini.

republika.description: Il coinvolgimento nel conflitto del passaggio verso il golfo di Aden farebbe schizzare i prezzi del greggio e della logistica

republika.description: Mattarella ha voluto una grande evento per coinvolgere il Paese. Cento le città collegate

republika.description: Il comandante solleva da compiti operativi gli agenti sospettati di avere innescato il putiferio. Ma sui fuochi di artificio all’origine del caos accusa: “Ogni anno li spara un corpo diverso”

npr.title: Global conflicts push Sri Lanka's economy to the brink
npr.description: Sri Lanka was careening from crisis to crisis, then came the Mideast war. People say they've got no buffer left.

npr.title: Ultra-Orthodox protesters block roads and trains across Israel over military draft
npr.description: Tens of thousands of ultra-Orthodox demonstrated across Israel on Monday, blocking roads and trains and setting cars on fire to protest mandatory enlistment in Israel's military.

npr.title: What to know about US military strikes on alleged drug boats
npr.description: The U.S. military strikes on alleged drug boats have killed over 200 people. The attacks began in September and aim to stem drug flow, but critics question their legality and effectiveness.

npr.title: Russian attack on Ukraine kills at least 14 and traps others in damaged buildings
npr.description: Russia launched hundreds of drones and dozens of missiles against Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities overnight, killing at least 14 civilians. Some people were trapped under the rubble of apartment buildings.

npr.title: Iran halts talks with U.S. over Israeli actions in Lebanon, Gaza
npr.description: Trumps says Israel and Hezbollah will stop fighting after Iran stops talks with U.S. over Israeli operations in southern Lebanon, Gaza

npr.title: U.S. strikes Iranian military sites. And, Trump's $1.8 billion fund faces scrutiny

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

undark.title: Medicine’s Move Toward Race-Neutral Risk Assessments
undark.description: Earlier this year, new guidelines were released for doctors assessing a patient’s risk for heart disease. The guidelines take a race-neutral and patient-informed approach that’s rooted in up-to-date science, one doctor writes, and offer a glimpse of a future in which health equity is the standard in medicine.

undark.title: In Coal Country, Black Lung Surges as Federal Protections Stall
undark.description: While the Trump administration is directing hundreds of millions of dollars to coal projects, miners in Appalachia are suffering from a resurgence of black lung disease. But industry pushback is delaying federal rules that would reduce miners’ exposure to deadly silica dust.

phys-org.title: Strange winds on seven hot Jupiters reveal strongest signs yet of exoplanet magnetic activity
phys-org.description: A team of astronomers has found the strongest evidence yet that some planets outside our solar system may be magnetic. Using the European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope (ESO's VLT) and the Gemini North telescope, the researchers measured wind speeds on seven very hot, Jupiter-like exoplanets.

phys-org.title: Biodiversity offsetting shows promise in pollinator conservation
phys-org.description: Newly created grassland habitats that compensate for nature lost to development can effectively support wild pollinators like bees and hoverflies, according to a first of its kind study in the Netherlands. The findings are published in the Journal of Applied Ecology.

phys-org.title: Making climate-neutral plastics and cosmetics using bacteria
phys-org.description: Plastics, medicines, cosmetics—there are very few everyday products that do not rely on using fossil resources. A European research team led by Charité—Universitätsmedizin Berlin is now aiming to revolutionize this cornerstone of the chemical industry: as part of the CarboNcare project, scientists are developing bacteria that can produce important chemical base materials from sustainable methanol—thereby replacing fossil resources.

phys-org.title: How the EU's carbon price on imports strengthens climate policies globally
phys-org.description: In early 2026, the EU extended its domestic carbon pricing to key products from beyond its borders. This is managed through the "Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism" (CBAM). Exporters of polluting goods to the EU must pay a climate tariff, unless their country has its own pricing scheme.

phys-org.title: ESA selects two new scout-class missions
phys-org.description: When it comes to understanding Earth and our changing environment, space is the place. Not only does it give us an overall holistic view of the planet below, but satellite-based imagery can transcend national boundaries and give us an understanding of key changes that often go unseen at ground level.

phys-org.description: The "soil" blanketing the moon's surface isn't actually soil. It's a fine, lethal, abrasive powder of shattered rock and jagged glass that shreds gaskets, chews through seals, and hangs in an airless environment blasted by unfiltered radiation and temperature swings that can warp steel. Scientists call it lunar regolith.

phys-org.description: Textile wastewater treatment practices inadvertently produce toxic byproducts—including chloroform and bromoform—at alarming levels that pose a clear occupational health hazard and lead to unknown environmental effects downstream, University of Massachusetts Amherst researchers have found. The study is published in the Journal of Hazardous Materials.

phys-org.title: Moderate thinning increased hair lichens, while heavy cuts reduced them in Sweden
phys-org.description: By using clearcutting, industrial forestry has caused a large-scale decline of hair lichens in Sweden's forests. In a large-scale field-experiment, researchers from Umeå University, University of Northern British Columbia, Canada, and Norwegian University of Life Sciences have shown that partial cutting can increase the abundance of hair lichens. The study is published in Forest Ecology and Management.

phys-org.title: First injured Langobard woman in skeletal record reshapes view of male-only violence
phys-org.description: The Langobards are frequently depicted as fierce warrior-like people, with all known archaeological evidence of violence restricted to men. However, nearly 1,400 years ago, a Langobard woman took two severe injuries to the head, one a clean slice made by a blade, the other a crushing blow, making her the first direct evidence of interpersonal violence in Langobard females.

phys-org.description: Conical intersections are crucial molecular switching points in light-driven reactions, but accurately predicting them usually requires computations. phys-org.title: Drought linked to 46% increase in sexual violence among adolescents in Southern Africa
phys-org.description: New research from the University of Oxford provides the first quantitative evidence that drought exposure over the last 12 months is associated with an increased risk of sexual, emotional and physical violence among adolescents in Southern Africa. This risk rises substantially during cumulative droughts over two years.

phys-org.title: Future jet stream changes could ease drying across Asian drylands
phys-org.description: Mid-latitude Asian drylands, stretching from Central Asia to northern China, are among the largest dryland systems in the world. Home to extensive agricultural activities and fragile ecosystems, the region is highly vulnerable to climate change and water scarcity.

phys-org.title: Bridged or not? Scientists uncover a key step in hydrogenase assembly
phys-org.description: How does nature build one of the most sophisticated catalytic metal centers found in biology? An international team of researchers has now resolved a long-standing debate surrounding the assembly of the active site of [FeFe]-hydrogenases—enzymes that rank among nature's most efficient catalysts for hydrogen production and consumption.

proj-syn.title: The One Man Who Could Give Trump Middle East Peace
proj-syn.description: With a large majority of UN member states recognizing Palestine on the 1967 lines, there is a clear international blueprint for creating an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel. What has been missing is credible Palestinian leadership of the kind that the imprisoned politician Marwan Barghouti could provide.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Nuclear Options
proj-syn.description: The risks raised by nuclear weapons remain as potent as ever, but the institutional framework that mitigated them has been severely eroded. The task now is to prevent deterrence from giving way to proliferation—which, for Europe, means building conventional capabilities, keeping the US engaged, and upholding restraint.

proj-syn.title: The Intelligence That AI Is Missing
proj-syn.description: For AI to simplify humans’ complex social and professional lives, it cannot just give tidy answers based on whatever the internet has to say about our values. It will need the capacity to account for our relational commitments, which are typically grounded in personal identity, experience, and culture.

proj-syn.title: Why Isn’t Europe Poorer Than the US?
proj-syn.description: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman has a point when he says that European living standards have largely kept pace with those in the US, despite flagging growth and innovation. But this will not remain true indefinitely: restoring Europe's ability to compete at the technological frontier remains essential to its future well-being.

proj-syn.title: The Real Choice Confronting Developing Countries
proj-syn.description: Lost in the debate about whether developing countries should pursue manufacturing- or services-led growth is the potential for new AI tools to make even informal workers far more productive. If governments can broaden access to such technologies, they no longer need to choose between strategies.

proj-syn.title: India’s Great Political Realignment
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party’s focus on religious identity, together with its “purification” of voter rolls, has created a more binary—and potentially volatile—political landscape, where elections increasingly reflect ethno-religious identity. This month’s elections in five states largely confirmed this trend.

proj-syn.title: Central Banking in an Age of Global Supply Shocks
proj-syn.description: The core assumptions underlying the decades-old inflation-targeting orthodoxy have proven to be unfit for a geopolitically fragmented world characterized by frequent supply-side disruptions. Under such conditions, central banks' traditional monetary policies are only as effective as markets believe them to be.

proj-syn.title: The Tech-MAGA Breakup Is Coming
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump has managed to fuse a backward-looking populist movement with a Silicon Valley vanguard whose guiding assumption is that AI will render a large share of ordinary people economically redundant. But with the tech billionaires now rewiring America's electricity grid and driving up costs, a split seems inevitable.

proj-syn.title: A Professor Should Work Hard and Grade Easy
proj-syn.description: The Harvard University faculty has now decided to limit the share of “A” grades given to students to about 20%. But, as the move's defenders freely admit, the intent is to increase professors' power and students' stress, not to generate excitement in the classroom.

proj-syn.title: What Price Hormuz?
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump has three primary objectives in the Persian Gulf: unwind the Iranian nuclear program, permanently reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and not be the president blamed for having “lost” Taiwan to China. The bad news for the US president is that he can achieve at most two of these goals.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasurement of Europe’s Productivity
proj-syn.description: The Nobel laureate economist Paul Krugman uses the wrong metric—purchasing power parity—to make the case that Europe is not lagging far behind the US in terms of productivity. The right metric shows that the gap is growing.

proj-syn.title: Latin America’s Agricultural Boom Is Faltering
proj-syn.description: The productivity growth that transformed agriculture across Latin America and the Caribbean has slowed sharply in recent years, with farmers increasingly relying on costly inputs rather than efficiency gains. Without sustained public investment, the region risks losing competitiveness and reversing decades of hard-won progress.

proj-syn.title: Americans Can’t Afford Trump’s Economy
proj-syn.description: Prices are rising faster than wages in the US, and President Donald Trump’s policies are a key reason why. Now is the time for the Democratic Party to advance a credible and specific “affordability platform” that addresses the biggest culprits, from tariffs and energy prices to mass deportation of immigrants.

proj-syn.title: Britain’s Center Cannot Hold
proj-syn.description: A combination of globalization, deindustrialization, and other forces destroyed the old model of party politics that long prevailed in developed democracies. Nowhere is this more apparent than in the United Kingdom, where voters are angry and demanding radical solutions that no political leader can actually deliver.

proj-syn.title: Reading Between China’s Red Lines
proj-syn.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping’s blunt warning to US President Donald Trump about Taiwan was clearly intended to sharpen the distinction between this ultimatum and the many others Xi has issued. But expanding the number of non-negotiable positions reduces the space for effective diplomacy and raises the risk of accidental conflict.

proj-syn.title: The Pope Should Have Gone Further on AI
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV has made waves with his first encyclical, in which he describes the development and deployment of new AI tools as a profound threat to human dignity. If anything, he has not gone far enough in pressing the question of what the technology is being designed to do.

proj-syn.title: China’s Long March to Technological Supremacy
proj-syn.description: China’s R&D prowess was visible in research output, patents, PhDs, and critical technologies for years, long before crystallizing into commercial products that Western investors, commentators, and policymakers noticed. And now it’s happening again.

proj-syn.title: The Pope’s Defense of Humanity
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV is right to celebrate the grandeur of humanity, to criticize and reject posthumanism, and to emphasize the essential, categorical, and insurmountable difference between humans and machines. His first encyclical is a necessary exhortation to believers and non-believers alike.
